title: tenant-weighted-slo-degradation-toggle-with-regional-escort-and-fastpatch
author: Asha Patel
description: Background: During recent cross-region incidents we observed tenants with bursty traffic causing disproportionate SLO churn for neighbouring tenants and triggering aggressive circuit flips. This PR introduces a tenant-weighted degradation toggle that lets the SLO enforcer gracefully apply partial degradation based on tenant weight and recent error budgets, plus a short-lived regional escort mechanism that moves affected requests to a holding pathway while circuits transfer state. Motivation: Reduce noisy reopen cycles and improve fairness during regional capacity pressure. Goals: 1) Allow operators to enable a tenant-weighted soft-degrade mode per-region; 2) Apply degradation in tiers based on tenant weight and remaining SLO budget; 3) Provide an ephemeral escort pathway that retains KV prefixes and routes requests to warm victims to avoid cold-start cascades; 4) Ship a fastpatch hotfix that fixes a regression in the circuit snapshot restore logic that caused stalled reopen attempts. Design summary: - New config toggle: region.slo.weighted_degrade: { enabled, tier_thresholds, max_degrade_pct } stored in feature flagging and surfaced in Console. - Per-tenant weight calculation: uses a rolling 1h token-weight window (weight = steady_qps + 2*burst_qps) with caps. - Degradation policy: tenants sorted by weight; degrade percentage applied from highest weight down until target CPU or SLO headroom is reclaimed. Degrading uses soft-paths (micro-evictions, reduced KV cache allocation, reduced batch size) rather than outright reject. - Regional escort pathway: short-lived worker pool that accepts in-progress requests from nodes undergoing circuit handoff. Escort replays prefix KV entries and keeps request latency bounded by throttling inbound concurrency. Escort state is ephemeral and auto-evicted after 60s. - Circuit snapshot fastpatch: fixes nil-check in snapshot restore during rapid reopen; patched logic adds a short randomized backoff prior to final snapshot apply. - Observability: added telemetry for tenant weight, degrade decisions, escort handoffs, snapshot errors. All events are tagged with region and circuit-id. Rollout plan and safety: - Feature default: disabled. Rollout steps: 1) Canary in us-west-2 on non-prod; 2) Gradual opt-in to 10% of traffic in PRODUCTION by tenant segments; 3) Monitor SLO delta and error budget bleed for 2 hours per step; 4) Full region enable if stable. - Fastpatch applied to main immediately and included in this PR; patch contains a hotfix-only commit and unit tests. - Rollback: toggle off and revert the fastpatch commit if snapshot issues reappear. Checklist: - [x] Core degrader algorithm implemented - [x] Escort worker + routing implemented - [x] Circuit snapshot nil-check hotfix included - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Metrics + logs added - [x] Console flag wiring and docs - [x] E2E scenario tests simulating region failover Related work: Linear ENG-9971 (slo fairness), PM-412 (console toggle UX). Support ticket SUP-1892 reported the original incident. Notes on backwards compatibility: No breaking changes to public API. Degradation is opt-in and conservative by default.

merge_commit_summary: Squash-merged tenant-weighted degrade + escort and snapshot fastpatch; adds metrics and console flag
review_comments: Linus Berg (2026-02-18): Can we avoid using wall-clock when computing the 1h window? Use monotonic clock to avoid skew on node restart. - Asha: switched to monotonic clock and added tests.

Riley Chen (2026-02-19): Concern: escort may increase tail latency under high contention. Suggest adding a soft concurrency cap and backpressure metric. - Asha: added concurrency cap (configurable, default 32) and metric escorts_in_flight.
Miguel Araujo (2026-02-20): Snapshot nil-check fix looks good, but add a randomized jitter to avoid thundering herd on restore. - Asha: added jittered backoff (10-200ms) and documented behavior.
Riley Chen (2026-02-22): Integration flake repro attached; fixed by adding a small sleep in test harness to allow KV warm-start. - Asha: updated e2e and re-ran CI; all green.
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in tenant-weighted SLO degradation mode and a regional escort pathway to reduce noisy circuit reopen cycles. Includes a fastpatch to fix a snapshot restore nil-pointer during rapid reopen. Default disabled; operators must enable per-region via Console.
changelog_entry: 2026-02-25 - Added tenant-weighted SLO soft-degrade toggle, regional escort pathway, and snapshot restore hotfix. Feature gated and off by default.
rollback_plan: 1) Disable region.slo.weighted_degrade toggle in Console. 2) Revert fastpatch commit if snapshot restores regress. 3) Rebalance traffic via routing policy to bypass affected region.
notes_for_oncall: If snapshot_restore_errors spike after rollout: 1) disable feature flag, 2) escalate to runtime on-call, 3) check escort queue length and escorts_in_flight metric, 4) if nodes show high stalled KV reads, run snapshot-verify utility. Fastpatch included in this PR is intended to prevent the nil-pointer path.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover weight calc and tier thresholds. Integration e2e exercises regional escort handoff; initial flake fixed. Load bench showed <2% throughput regression at target degrade settings. Canary run in staging for 48h with no SLO regressions.
security_considerations: No new surface exposed externally. Escort pathway runs inside existing regional worker pool and obeys auth/authz. Telemetry uses existing redact rules; no PII added.
